card.title: Steer the Suspicion
card.instruction: Hide your responsibility by redirecting every new clue toward a safer explanation before anyone can connect it back to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your shelf fell because they supplied the wrong bracket.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You fitted it upside down. Look at the arrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a misleading arrow. We should photograph it for the manufacturer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You drew that arrow. I watched you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because theirs was missing. Put that in the complaint; they made us supply our own safety markings.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 blames bracket supply; A3 blames the arrow and A5 makes A's own drawing evidence of manufacturer omission.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 upside-down fitting and arrow prompt A3 marking complaint; B4 A drew it prompts A5 missing original marks.

relationship.evidence: B2 identifies installation error and B4 personally witnessed the drawing, making B a credible observer.

heightening.evidence: B4 removes manufacturer authorship of the arrow; A5 reverses that loss into the manufacturer's failure to supply one.

specificity.evidence: A1 fallen shelf and B2 bracket arrow give a concrete repair mistake and responsibility dispute.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 they made us supply our own safety markings turns the strongest incriminating clue into a complaint.
